1.explanation:
• docs/reveal/index.qmd shows how the revealjs format is set up and renders slides; it’s the template context in which embed should work.
• docs/reveal/mini/auto-animate-code.qmd demonstrates code display within a mini revealjs example and lets you compare how normal code chunks are handled vs. embed chunks.
• docs/test-singleformat-html.qmd is the comparable non-reveal HTML example that successfully shows embedded code; useful as a control to reproduce the working case.
• docs/test-knitr-options.qmd contains examples of knitr engine usage in Quarto, helping to verify that the knitr engine is otherwise functioning and to compare options.
• docs/code-tools/code-tools-external-source.qmd shows including external code through the code-tools mechanism; this is a close parallel to embed (including from a file) and useful to inspect how external sources are injected into HTML vs. revealjs.
• docs/bug-repros/issue-1340/index.qmd is a minimal bug repro in QMD form that you can adapt to reproduce the embed issue and compare with other known bug repro patterns.
1.bug_scenario:
When rendering a Quarto document with format: revealjs and engine: knitr, an `{embed, file='code.R'}` chunk yields an empty `
` rather than showing the contents of code.R. In contrast, rendering the same embed chunk to standard HTML (without revealjs) correctly shows the embedded code. The bug scenario involves the revealjs slide background, the slide wrapper `
` element, and the empty cell `
` where the code should appear.
